page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is a compute-oriented virtual machine within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical AMD EPYC processor cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is provisioned with 32.0 GB of memory, resulting in a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core, 16 MB of L3 cache, and instruction set support for AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2. An integrated 300 GB NVMe solid-state drive handles local disk operations, and one complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned. No dedicated GPU accelerators are attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread efficiency alongside reliable multi-core throughput. Single-core performance registered within the top 25 percent across both stress-ng (2,935.67) and Geekbench (2,168.0), driven by solid instructions-per-clock execution despite the moderate 2.0 GHz base frequency. Multi-core compute scaled to 46,446.97 in stress-ng and 15,777.0 in Geekbench, placing it in the median performance tier. In specialized computational evaluations, the instance showed top-quartile results in Geekbench text and image processing, as well as top-decile text generation speed on smaller 135M parameter language models at 347.96 tokens per second. Memory bandwidth measured 149.65 GB/sec for large uncached block reads, while PassMark database operations and Redis SET throughput aligned with median tier expectations.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio maximizes CPU allocation per unit of RAM, establishing high cost efficiency for computationally bound tasks that do not require massive resident memory pools. However, the absence of AVX-512 and AMX extensions constrains throughput on matrix-heavy machine learning training, and the 32.0 GB ceiling makes it less suitable for large in-memory databases. Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is primarily suited for continuous integration build runners, compiling software with Clang, batch processing, static web serving, and lightweight CPU-based language model inference.
description: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs backed by 8 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with a compute-focused 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, it delivers strong single-core throughput, ranking in the upper quartile for both Geekbench and stress-ng single-thread tests. Its multi-core throughput and memory subsystems demonstrate balanced performance across software compilation, web serving, and cryptographic tasks. The bundled high-speed NVMe storage provides low-latency local I/O, while the CPU architecture includes hardware-level AES and AVX acceleration. While memory-dense workloads and deep learning training are constrained by the 32 GB RAM envelope and lack of AVX-512 extensions, this server offers robust resource density for CI/CD pipelines, Clang software builds, web serving, and lightweight language model inference.
